title: Enter the skill contest?
hook: Could confidence in your skill still lead to too much entry?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish absolute ability from ability relative to the competitors who also enter.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish absolute ability from ability relative to the competitors who also enter.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: Your toy contest score is eighty and your rival scores ninety. What is your winning margin? Toy inputs A=[80, 90]; B=[80, 70].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[-10, 80, 90], [10, 80, 70]]. Labels: Winning margin, Your score, Rival score.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The same personal performance can win or lose depending on who else enters. The two cases keep your ability fixed and change the competitive environment. Absolute skill is therefore not enough to calculate the chance of winning.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Your score=80, Rival score=70. What is Winning margin? Answer: 10.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Your score=80, Rival score=70. What is Winning margin?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 10. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: People enter competitions too often when success depends on their own skill, ignoring how good rivals are (Camerer & Lovallo, 1999).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish absolute ability from ability relative to the competitors who also enter.
